title: Integrated Financial Planning, Procurement & Revenue Recognition Playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook documents Redwood Inference's integrated approach to: (1) annual and rolling budgeting and forecasting, (2) contract intake and legal review, (3) procurement and purchasing approvals, and (4) revenue recognition and billing controls. It consolidates procedures, thresholds, ownership, and templates to ensure consistent decisions across finance, legal, procurement, and product teams.

Scope

- Applies to all corporate spend, supplier contracts, customer contracts, and revenue arrangements impacting Redwood Inference consolidated financial statements and operational budgets.
- Excludes personal expense reimbursements (see Expense Reimbursement Policy) and recruiting/vendor-sourcing procedures owned by People Ops.

Objectives

- Ensure budget accuracy and rolling forecast cadence aligned to product roadmaps and capacity plans.
- Maintain legal and compliance guardrails for contracts with SLAs, indemnities, and data residency clauses.
- Enforce procurement approval thresholds to control spend and vendor risk.
- Provide clear revenue recognition criteria consistent with ASC 606 principles and Redwood billing processes.

Roles and ownership

- CFO (owner): final approval authority for annual budget and high-risk supplier engagements.
- VP Finance (planning lead): owns forecasting cadence, variance analysis, and budget consolidation.
- Legal Counsel (contracts lead): owns contract templates, legal reviews, and redline authority.
- Procurement Manager: manages vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and supplier risk assessments.
- Revenue Operations Manager: owns billing controls, invoice issuance, and RevRec documentation.
- Product & Eng partners: provide capacity forecasts, cost drivers (GPU hours, storage, network), and feature rollout dates for forecasting.

Budgeting & Forecasting process

Cadence

1. Annual budget: starts in October, draft delivered to leadership by November 15, board package produced by December 15.
2. Quarterly rolling forecast: updated within 10 business days after quarter close.
3. Monthly forecast refresh: top-line and major cost centers (hosting, R&D, sales) updated by 7th business day.

Inputs and assumptions

- Revenue: deal pipeline (sales), usage growth rates for hosted API, Dedicated commitments, Private deployment contract timings.
- Cost of Goods Sold (COGS): GPU fleet cost, cloud egress, model licensing fees, and third-party service charges.
- Operating expenses: headcount plans by team, third-party contracts, marketing programs.

Deliverables

- Budget workbook (master tab) with driver-based sections: revenue drivers, unit economics (ARPU, cost-per-token, embedding cost), capital vs. opex split.
- Forecast variance report with explanations for >5% variance vs prior.

Approval matrix and thresholds

| Item | Approval required | Approver | SLA for decision |
|------|------------------|---------|------------------|
| Spend up to $25k | Procurement Manager | Procurement Manager | 3 business days |
| Spend $25k-$250k | VP Finance + Procurement Manager | VP Finance | 5 business days |
| Spend > $250k | CFO + Legal (if contract) | CFO | 10 business days |

Contracts & legal process

Contract intake

1. Sales / Procurement submit Request for Contract (RFC) via Contract Intake form (Confluence link and JIRA intake) with: counterparty name, contract type, value, term, data residency needs, indemnity/limitation requests, and required signatures.
2. Legal triages RFC within 2 business days; high-risk tags: data processing, HIPAA, SOC2 customer, export controls.

Standard templates and redlines

- Use the approved Master Services Agreement (MSA) or Supplier Agreement template located at /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/templates.
- Allowed commercial deviations: payment term change up to net-45, minor limitation of liability adjustments within pre-approved caps (see table below). Any other deviation requires Legal Counsel sign-off.

Commercial deviation thresholds

| Clause | Allowed deviation without CFO sign-off | Requires CFO sign-off | Requires Exec review |
|--------|----------------------------------------|-----------------------|----------------------|
| Payment terms | Up to net-45 | net-60 | >90 days |
| Liability cap | Up to 6 months of expected fees | 6-12 months | >12 months |
| Data residency | None (use standard region) | Additional region | Requires Security & Legal review |

Contract execution flow

1. Legal completes redline and commercial review within 5 business days for standard agreements.
2. If negotiation extends, escalate to Legal Lead and Procurement Manager at day 7.
3. Signatures: Electronic signature via DocuSign; Authorized signatories list maintained by Finance.

Procurement procedures

Vendor selection and onboarding

- Competitive sourcing required for contracted spend > $50k annually. Procurement issues RFQ/RFP to minimum 3 vendors.
- Vendor risk assessment (data access, financial health, security posture, SOC2) completed prior to PO issuance.

Purchase order (PO) and payment

1. Create a PO in the procurement system (NetSuite / Coupa) with GL codes provided by Finance.
2. PO approval required per thresholds table above.
3. Supplier invoice matched to PO; exceptions routed to Accounts Payable within 3 business days.

Lead times and SLAs

- PO issuance SLA: 5 business days after final contract or approval.
- Invoice payment SLA: net terms (default net-30); early payment discounts should be evaluated for >$100k payments.

Procurement exceptions

- Ad-hoc non-PO purchases below $2k may be made with card, but cardholder must submit receipts and reconcile within 5 business days.
- Single-source vendor >$50k must have documented justification and Procurement Manager approval.

Revenue recognition & billing policy (summary)

Principles

- Follow ASC 606: identify contract(s) with customer, determine performance obligations, transaction price, allocation, and recognize revenue as obligations are satisfied.
- Revenue recognized over time when customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefits (e.g., hosted API with usage billing) or at a point in time for one-off professional services.

Key rules and examples

- Subscription/Committed Dedicated Capacity: recognize ratably over the committed period when capacity is reserved and service is continuously provided.
- Usage-based hosted API: recognize as usage is realized (measured tokens/embedding units) in the period the usage occurs.
- Multi-element arrangements: allocate transaction price using standalone selling price hierarchy; document estimates and any discounts.

Controls and documentation

- Revenue Accounting checklist required for all customer contracts: contract copy, signed MSA, SOW/ordering docs, pricing schedule, and implementation milestones.
- Revenue recognition entries must be supported by system reports: billing ledger, usage logs (token counts), and customer invoices.

Billing operations SLAs & accuracy targets

- Invoice issuance: All monthly invoices sent within 5 business days of month close.
- Billing accuracy: target 99.9% line-item accuracy; material errors (>0.5% of monthly revenue) trigger investigation.
- DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) target: 30 days for net-30 customers; escalate >60 days to Collections.

Operational checklist (pre-approval and month close)

Pre-approval (before signing a contract or issuing a PO)

- Confirm budget/forecast capacity: the spend is included in current budget or has an approved budget amendment.
- Complete vendor risk assessment for suppliers with data access.
- Legal review completed; commercial deviations documented.
- Procurement approvals per threshold matrix obtained.

Month close checklist (Finance & RevOps)

1. Reconcile usage logs to billed amounts; investigate variances >1%.
2. Accrue deferred revenue for prepaid or contracted committed capacity.
3. Post revenue recognition journal entries with supporting evidence attached in the accounting system.
4. Run invoicing batch and confirm invoices delivered; log failed deliveries and reissue within 2 business days.

Change control and exceptions

- Any change that impacts revenue recognition policy or material budget deltas (>5% of department budget) requires VP Finance approval and Legal notification.
- Emergency procurements (safety, urgent infra) must be logged and reviewed post-facto within 10 business days.

Templates and appendices

- Contract Intake form: link to Confluence template (RFC + required attachments).
- Approved MSA and Supplier Agreement templates.
- Vendor Risk Assessment checklist (security, financial, legal).
- Budget workbook template and forecast driver tab (sample).
- Revenue accounting checklist (fields required for RevRec sign-off).
